newsitem.title: IRAN: Khatami calls on Iranians to respect majority vote.
newsitem.headline: Khatami calls on Iranians to respect majority vote.

text.p: Iran's president-elect Mohammad Khatami on Saturday called upon all Iranians to respect the vote of the majority which gave him a wide margin of victory in May elections.
"Everybody in the country should respect the vote of the majority of the Iranian people," Khatami said in his first televised speech to Iranians.
Khatami, a former culture minister, said ministers in his future cabinet would be "powerful, innovative, fresh-minded and devoted to the country's development, justice and independence."
Iranian newspapers have said that Khatami was being pressured by conservatives over the choice of ministers.
Conservative Shi'ite Moslem clerics, whose candidate, Parliament Speaker Ali Akbar Nateq Nouri lost to Khatami in the polls, have demanded they be consulted over the choice of ministers.
The conservatives have a majority in the Majlis, or parliament, and could block candidates submitted by Khatami who was elected by nearly 70 percent of some 29 million votes.
Khatami has said he would look beyond factional barriers in picking his cabinet. He will be sworn in as president of the Islamic republic on August 3.
